Check for minimum, maximum and other single-person values

check_extremes.Rd

Minimum and maximum values almost always belong to one person. This check looks for them by name: column names, row names, names of a vector and character cells such as "Max." in a statistics column (for example output from summary()).

Usage

check_extremes(x, config = NULL, target = NULL)

Arguments

x

A data frame, table, matrix or named vector.

config

A mimic_config(); NULL uses the defaults.

target

Label used in reports.

Value

A mimic_check listing where extremes were found.

See also

Other checks: check_differencing(), check_dominance(), check_group_disclosure(), check_k_anonymity(), check_keys(), check_min_count(), check_model(), check_suppression()

Examples

check_extremes(summary(fake_persons$income))
#> ✖ extremes (summary(fake_persons$income)): Found 2 minimum, maximum or range value(s). These are often one person's value.
#>  location name
#>      name Min.
#>      name Max.
check_extremes(data.frame(group = "a", mean = 1, max_income = 2))
#> ✖ extremes (data.frame(group = "a", mean = 1, max...): Found 1 minimum, maximum or range value(s). These are often one person's value.
#>  location       name
#>    column max_income
